_comment: What each corpus file must yield once the whole extraction pipeline has run:
preextract.ts converts, enrich.py indexes, and these are assertions on the text
the fts5 words table ends up holding, which is what search and chat read.
Assertions are properties, not golden files. Converter output legitimately
shifts between downmark releases (spacing, table padding, a heading level);
byte-exact goldens would churn on every bump and train everyone to re-bless
them without looking. These say what must never stop being true: the content
is present, and the structure that the old flat-text readers destroyed
survived. `absent` catches the specific regressions we have already had.

docs/handbook.docx.why: Headings and tables: the structure python-docx flattened to tab-joined lines.

docs/quarterly.xlsx.why: Every sheet becomes its own heading plus a Markdown table.

docs/kickoff.pptx.why: Slide boundaries, the table, and speaker notes; the old reader dropped all three.
contains: Speaker note: mention the rerun policy.

docs/report.pdf.why: An ordinary typeset PDF: both pages present, and no OCR was needed for it.

notes/readme.md.why: Markdown is read as-is, not converted.
contains: The refinement pass follows the handbook.

notes/runs.csv.why: Plain text formats keep flowing through enrich.py untouched.

notes/settings.json.why: JSON is indexed as text; the viewer renders it as a tree separately.

notes/postprocess.py.why: Source files are part of the corpus and must not be skipped.
